answers:
1. The one I can point to for sure is the elephant toothpaste demo. I've done it every year since my first, and it always goes well. I don't have a specific lesson that went badly that I can name right now, so I'd skip that half.

2. I don't have a particular question I can pin down, so I'd rather skip this one. I don't want to invent one.

3. Honestly, I can't name a specific student I was wondering about that day. Amina Yusuf did show up, though, a former student who's a pharmacist now, and she brought her young daughter to watch. So I was wondering about students like her, where they ended up.

4. I don't remember the exact date, so I'll leave that out. What I hadn't planned on was Amina turning up with her daughter during my last class, period 4 AP Chemistry.

5. I don't remember what the last thing I picked up was, so I'd skip that. I ended with the elephant toothpaste demo, and I'll admit I felt relieved as much as sad, which is a little embarrassing. I also have no real plan for what comes next.

On my last day at Lakeview High, after 31 years of teaching chemistry, I straightened the lab stools, checked the taps, and wiped down a bench that was already clean. I had thought of retirement for so long as a date on the calendar that I never considered how I would actually leave the room.

What I hadn't planned on was Amina Yusuf turning up during my last class, period 4 AP Chemistry. She's a pharmacist now, and she brought her young daughter to watch. Seeing her made me wonder about all the students like her, where they ended up.

I ended with the elephant toothpaste demo, which I've done every year since my first and which has always gone well. I felt relieved as much as sad, which is a little embarrassing. I have no real plan for what comes next.
</final>
